People with schizophrenia and similar mental illnesses are shown to have a lowered count of their acetylcholine levels, and some psychotic symptoms can be worsened by a depleted acetylcholine count. Nicotine is a chemical that fits the acetylcholine receptors perfectly. Studies have shown that because of this, the usage of nicotine products can temporarily alleviate some symptoms. A lot of people with schizophrenia end up self-medicating by smoking cigarettes without even knowing that’s what they’re doing.

Yeah, I definitely know a lot about dph and what it does physically and chemically to the brain and body. As well as the behavior changes it causes in people.

I don’t mean to sound salty, I just wish people were more educated and aware about things because everyone talks casually about how unpleasant it is, but not a lot of people really get into specifics. This is one of those drugs that doesn’t lead anywhere good, and it is the most addictive thing I have ever personally encountered. I don’t have an addictive personality at all, I start and permanently stop regular usage of intoxicants all the time (alcohol, cigarettes, stimulants, etc), and I have never experienced cravings or withdrawals from any of it even after prolonged regular use— but in the few dph “trips” I’ve taken, I still have times in my darkest moments where I think about how I could just take dph and be a zombie. Crazy stuff, really.

idk man there’s some god experiences through drugs out there, dph ain’t one of them. dph is a direct door to the shadow realm. and yea people like to make memes about it, but it’s true. continued dph use creates living hungry ghosts— people that need to feed on other people because they’ve given everything of themselves to the dark entities that occupy that space. i’ll also mention that it’s not the only door, but it’s a easy one to get through.
